events.title: US CPI (September) release
events.expected_direction: bearish if hot, bullish if cool
events.why_it_matters: Last inflation print before the Oct 28 FOMC; markets price a possible Fed hike, so a hot print would hit bonds and equities.
events.what_to_watch: Core CPI m/m vs ~0.3% consensus and supercore services.

events.title: FOMC rate decision (Oct 27-28)
events.why_it_matters: Fed under Chair Kevin Warsh is signaling another hike (Sept minutes lean hawkish); the hike-or-hold decision is the month's biggest macro risk.
events.what_to_watch: CPI Oct 14 and Warsh's speech this week as the decision inputs.

events.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speech this week
events.why_it_matters: Bond traders are explicitly awaiting Warsh's remarks for insight on the October rate path.
events.what_to_watch: Hawkish language on inflation vs any signal of a pause.

events.title: Q3 bank earnings kickoff: JPM, GS, C
events.why_it_matters: Kicks off Q3 season; record trading may offset margin pressure from rising yields, with dealmaking outlook in focus.
events.what_to_watch: Net interest income guidance and capital-markets commentary.
sources: https://www.reuters.com (US bank investors to focus on impact of higher rates)

events.title: Healthcare and consumer earnings: UNH, JNJ, Domino's
events.why_it_matters: UNH and JNJ are sector bellwethers; UNH particularly sensitive to policy/market sentiment after its volatile 2025-26.
events.what_to_watch: Medical cost trends and 2026 guidance reaffirmations.

events.title: TSMC Q3 record revenue beat (resolved, momentum continues)
events.why_it_matters: TSMC's record Q3 and Samsung's ~9x profit jump confirm the AI chip/memory trade is intact, supporting global semis.
events.what_to_watch: TSMC capex guidance and NVDA put/call skew ahead of its own results.
sources: https://www.reuters.com (TSMC third-quarter revenue surges to record)

events.title: Iran war and Strait of Hormuz oil disruption
events.expected_direction: bearish for broad market, bullish for energy
events.why_it_matters: The ongoing Iran war keeps Gulf oil exports constrained, fuel prices elevated, and inflation expectations sticky — directly feeding the Fed's hawkish problem.
events.what_to_watch: Escalation incidents, tanker traffic through Hormuz, diesel/gasoline prices.
sources: https://www.nytimes.com (World's Energy Order Tested Again as Iran War's Reach Extends Further)
https://www.aljazeera.com (What the Iran war has done to the world's energy supply)

events.title: OPEC+ keeps November quotas unchanged
events.why_it_matters: OPEC+ paused output increases through end-2026 amid Hormuz disruptions, adding no barrels and keeping crude supported.
events.what_to_watch: Next monthly OPEC+ meeting and compliance with quotas.

events.title: White House emergency diesel fuel tax relief EO 14435
events.why_it_matters: Executive action to relieve diesel costs for farmers signals White House alarm over fuel prices from the Iran war — partial fiscal offset to energy inflation.
events.what_to_watch: Whether further fuel-relief or SPR measures follow.

events.title: US-China Board of Trade mechanism / truce extension
events.why_it_matters: Trump-Xi Washington meeting (Sept 24-25) extended the trade truce ~2 months and launched product-list tariff cuts, but it is fragile and expires soon.
events.what_to_watch: Product-list implementation, rare-earth export licensing, any truce breakdown headlines.
sources: https://www.nytimes.com (U.S. and China Agree to Extend Trade Truce by 2 Months)

events.title: CBP declaration responding to Sept 17 court order on tariffs
events.why_it_matters: Post-SCOTUS IEEPA strike-down, litigation over replacement tariff authorities continues; court-ordered changes to tariff collection create refund/refund-mechanics and trade uncertainty.
events.what_to_watch: Further court rulings and CBP implementation guidance.

events.title: EU-China trade talks in Beijing (rare earths, EV curbs)
events.why_it_matters: Talks over rare-earth export controls and hybrid-car curbs affect European automakers and global chip/materials supply chains.
events.what_to_watch: Any rare-earth licensing concessions or EU retaliation.
sources: https://www.brusselstimes.com (EU-China trade talks grapple with tariffs, rare earths, export controls)
https://www.aljazeera.com (EU-China trade talks begin in Beijing)

events.title: Eurozone inflation at 3.8%; ECB seen hiking in December
events.why_it_matters: HICP near double the 2% target has markets pricing another ECB hike in December, pressuring eurozone bonds and French spreads.
events.what_to_watch: Next eurozone CPI flash (late October) and French OAT yields.
sources: https://www.reuters.com (POLL ECB to hike rates again in December)

events.title: Bank of Japan decision Oct 29-30; hiked to 1.25% in September
events.why_it_matters: BOJ raised rates to 1.25% on Sept 24; a further hike or hawkish signals would move the yen and global carry trades.
events.what_to_watch: US-Japan trade/rare-earth friction (Takaichi angle) and Japan inflation prints.

events.title: US government funded through Dec 11; shutdown averted
events.why_it_matters: CR signed Sept 2 funds the government to Dec 11 — no shutdown risk in this window, but a December cliff looms right after the midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Appropriations negotiations and any pre-election brinkmanship.

events.title: IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings + October WEO
events.why_it_matters: IMF WEO (Oct 13) lifted 2026 global growth to 3.1% but warns the economy 'could soon test the limits of resilience' on energy and fiscal risks; meetings in Bangkok shape policy dialogue.
events.what_to_watch: WEO chapter details on energy constraints and fiscal risk warnings.

events.title: Hurricane Isaias Gulf Coast landfall (Oct 9)
events.why_it_matters: First US hurricane since 2024 hit the Gulf with storm surge and flooding — insurance losses, refining/energy infrastructure checks, and reconstruction demand follow.
events.what_to_watch: Insured-loss estimates and any refinery/Gulf port disruption.

events.title: AI sentiment wobble: OpenAI headlines pressure tech
events.why_it_matters: Negative OpenAI-related news is weighing on the AI trade just as NVDA options positioning shows elevated hedging — tech is the market's leadership and fragile to sentiment shifts.
events.what_to_watch: NVDA/semis price action and any hyperscaler capex commentary this earnings season.
sources: https://realinvestmentadvice.com (OpenAI Rains On The Tech Parade)

events.title: Section 301 forced-labor tariffs on 60 economies active
events.why_it_matters: 10-12.5% tariffs on 60 economies remain in force after the IEEPA ruling — the primary surviving tariff authority feeding into costs and inflation.
events.what_to_watch: Further Section 301 investigations (structural excess capacity) and importer litigation.

events.title: US 2026 midterm elections (Nov 3) ramp-up
events.why_it_matters: Final weeks of the midterm campaign increase risk of politically driven policy announcements (tariffs, fiscal goodies, investigations) and raise post-election regime uncertainty.
events.what_to_watch: Polling shifts, campaign fiscal/tariff pledges, and the Dec 11 funding deadline framing.

events.title: CIT certifies importer class action for IEEPA tariff refunds
events.why_it_matters: First-ever class certification in a tariff refund case opens the door to a potentially massive (multi-billion) refund liability for the government after the SCOTUS IEEPA strike-down.
events.what_to_watch: Government appeal or settlement posture; combined Amazon refund suits in D.C. federal court as a parallel track.

events.title: CFTC launches crypto market-structure rulemaking alongside SEC digital-asset framework
events.why_it_matters: Parallel CFTC/SEC rulemaking on digital assets will define SEC-vs-CFTC jurisdiction and compliance burdens for exchanges and stablecoin issuers while the CLARITY Act sits in the Senate.
events.what_to_watch: Comment periods and any exemptive relief timing; crypto exchange listings/stocks (COIN, HOOD) reaction.

events.title: FTC investigating OpenAI, Anthropic over consumer harms
events.why_it_matters: Direct regulatory pressure on the AI leaders compounds the same-week AI sentiment wobble and raises tail risk for the entire AI trade.
events.what_to_watch: CID scope, any House/agency coordination, and whether probes expand to other AI labs.

events.title: 30-year Treasury auction at 5.618% — highest since 2000
events.why_it_matters: Long-end yields at 25-year highs with a 2.54 cover on the 30-year signal strained demand amid hawkish-Fed and energy-inflation pricing — a headwind for equities and housing.
events.what_to_watch: Next refunding cycle and how the long end trades into the Oct 14 CPI and Oct 28 FOMC.

events.title: Initial jobless claims fall to 197k — lowest since July
events.expected_direction: bearish for bonds, unclear for equities
events.why_it_matters: Tight labor data supports the Fed's hawkish case going into the Oct 28 FOMC, reinforcing hike pricing.
events.what_to_watch: Thursday claims print (Oct 15) for confirmation ahead of CPI-adjacent positioning.

events.title: EIA natural gas storage +85 Bcf; stocks 2% above 5-yr average
events.why_it_matters: Adequate pre-winter gas supply is a partial offset to the Iran-war-driven energy complex and keeps heating-season price risk contained.
events.what_to_watch: Weekly builds vs 5-yr average and cold-weather forecasts into November.

top_risks: Hot CPI (Oct 14) confirms another Fed hike on Oct 28 — double hit to bonds and rate-sensitive equities
Iran war escalation or Hormuz closure spikes oil and entrenches inflation
US-China trade truce expires/fragile; rare-earth export controls re-escalate
AI/tech sentiment crack (OpenAI headlines, NVDA positioning) given narrow market leadership
December 11 government funding cliff and midterm-driven political volatility
top_opportunities: TSMC/Samsung record results confirm AI hardware demand — semis momentum
OPEC+ quota pause + Hormuz disruption keeps Energy sector earnings strong
Cool CPI would flip markets to dovish repricing before the FOMC
US-China tariff-cut product lists could relieve importers and consumer names
Hurricane reconstruction and insurance repricing plays
summary: The dominant macro setup: a hawkish Fed under Warsh deciding Oct 28 with the Oct 14 CPI as the swing input, against an oil market squeezed by the ongoing Iran war and OPEC+ quota pauses. The US-China truce holds for now but is fragile, while AI-leadership equities face sentiment wobbles despite stellar TSMC/Samsung results. No shutdown in this window (CR runs to Dec 11), but midterms amplify political headline risk.

catcher.coverage_assessment: The primary covered macro, energy-geopolitics, and earnings thoroughly, but missed judicial developments on tariff refunds (class certification), the CFTC/SEC crypto rulemaking push, the FTC AI probe, and the bond-market signal of 25-year-high 30-year yields.
catcher.biggest_gap: Trade Court certification of the importer class seeking IEEPA tariff refunds — potentially billions in fiscal liability and a major trade-policy overhang the primary only touched via the CBP declaration.
